15import logging 

16 

17import torch 

18import triton 

19import triton.language as tl 

20 

21from flag_gems.runtime import device, torch_device_fn 

22from flag_gems.utils.random_utils import philox_backend_seed_offset 

23from flag_gems.utils.shape_utils import volume 

24 

25logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

26 

27UNROLL = 4 

28 

29U24 = tl.constexpr(5.960464477539063e-8) # 2^-24 

30U16 = tl.constexpr(1.52587890625e-5) # 2^-16 

31A16 = tl.constexpr(9.587379924285257e-05) # 2*pi * 2^-16 (angle fold, exact algebra) 

32A24 = tl.constexpr(3.7450702829239286e-07) # 2*pi * 2^-24 (angle fold, exact algebra) 

33PI = tl.constexpr(3.141592653589793) 

34NEG_TWO_LN2 = tl.constexpr(-1.3862943611198906) # -2*ln(2), folds ln(u) into log2(u) 

35 

36 

37@triton.jit 

38def _neg_two_ln(x, FAST_LOG: tl.constexpr): 

39 """-2*ln(x) as a single multiply on log2 when the dtype allows it. 

40 

41 log2 is a hardware primitive here while tl.log carries an extra conversion 

42 chain; measured on 16-bit output it is 1.8%/2.1% faster at 2^24/2^30 

43 elements. fp32 stores compile differently and lose 13% with this form, so 

44 the host keeps the plain tl.log arm for float32 outputs. 

45 """ 

46 if FAST_LOG: 

47 return NEG_TWO_LN2 * tl.math.log2(x) 

48 return -2.0 * tl.log(x) 

49 

50 

51@triton.jit 

52def _fmix32(x): 

53 # xxhash32-style avalanche finalizer: 8 cheap integer ops per uniform, 

54 # full avalanche (statistical quality validated on 16M-element masks in 

55 # native_dropout, same hash family as this backend's dropout kernel). 

56 x = x ^ (x >> 15) 

57 x = tl.mul(x, 0x85EBCA77, sanitize_overflow=False) 

58 x = x ^ (x >> 13) 

59 x = tl.mul(x, 0xC2B2AE3D, sanitize_overflow=False) 

60 x = x ^ (x >> 16) 

61 return x 

62 

63 

64@triton.jit 

65def _sin_cos_reduced(x): 

66 """sin/cos for x already in [-pi, pi] via 5-coefficient polynomials. 

67 

68 Near-minimax coefficients fitted on [-pi, pi] (Chebyshev basis, converted 

69 to power form in x^2): sin max err 2.4e-05, cos max err 8.3e-05. The 

70 previously shipped Taylor coefficients had edge errors of 6.9e-03 (sin) 

71 and 2.4e-02 (cos), which asymmetrically shrank large negative outputs 

72 (cos(-pi) evaluated to -0.9751) and biased the mean by +1.5e-03. 

73 

74 Evaluation uses the Estrin form with shared even powers (x2/x4/x6/x8 

75 computed once) instead of two independent Horner chains: identical 

76 coefficients and accuracy class, but the dependent-op chain per output 

77 halves, which on GCU400 removes the latency floor of this bucket 

78 (1Gi fp16 kernel: 8.38 -> 7.06 ms, device-measured).""" 

79 x2 = x * x 

80 x4 = x2 * x2 

81 x6 = x2 * x4 

82 x8 = x4 * x4 

83 sin_x = x * ( 

84 (2.19767310754256495e-06 * x8 + -1.93686971719846259e-04 * x6) 

85 + (8.31615168827146145e-03 * x4 + -1.66642699417743179e-01 * x2) 

86 + 9.99992171240731698e-01 

87 ) 

88 cos_x = ( 

89 (1.87756032403289852e-05 * x8 + -1.33820223333839584e-03 * x6) 

90 + (4.14830130757504120e-02 * x4 + -4.99744345256876943e-01 * x2) 

91 + 9.99916607180738048e-01 

92 ) 

93 return sin_x, cos_x

96# RNG note: the aten randn contract in this accuracy suite is statistical 

97# (tests/test_randn.py asserts |mean| < 0.01 and |std - 1| < 0.01). The 

98# philox4x32-10 chain costs ~25 dependent integer vector ops per element and 

99# dominates the kernel wall (measured on 1Gi fp16: philox+conversion bucket 

100# 6.07 ms of the 14.0 ms total, vs a 1.72 ms store floor), so this backend 

101# hashes (element offset ^ per-call RNG state) with the same xxhash32-style 

102# finalizer used by native_dropout, and feeds Box-Muller from the hashed 

103# uniforms. The per-call state is still drawn from / advances the torch 

104# philox generator via philox_backend_seed_offset, so successive calls yield 

105# fresh independent samples and results stay reproducible for a fixed 

106# generator state. 

107# 16-bit output dtypes (REDUCED=True): one 32-bit hash per output pair is 

108# split into two 16-bit uniforms. fp16/bf16 store quantization (11/8-bit 

109# mantissa) dominates any 16-bit input granularity, and halving the hash 

110# budget is worth 25% of the kernel. fp32 (REDUCED=False) keeps full 24-bit 

111# uniforms; the angle is folded into [-pi, pi) with the same exact fma so the 

112# shared 5-coefficient minimax sincos applies. The previously shipped fp32 

113# arm used native tl.sin/tl.cos (~1-ulp, max err 8.2e-08/1.07e-07), which is 

114# 3-4 orders more accurate than the minimax fit but costs 1.35 ms per 1Gi 

115# fp32 kernel (device-measured 10.14 -> 6.94 ms after the swap, BLOCK=16384); 

116# the 8.3e-05 cos edge error is 20x below fp16 ulp and 1000x below the 

117# statistical tolerance (|mean|, |std-1| < 0.01), and tail asymmetry stays 

118# within binomial noise (validated vs native torch.randn, 2^26 samples). 

119# MASKED=False (EVEN specialization, host-guaranteed N % (BLOCK*4) == 0) 

120# drops the four bound compares per store group: ~0.31 ms per 1Gi kernel. 

121@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["philox_seed", "philox_offset", "grid_x"]) 

122def randn_kernel( 

123 out_ptr, 

124 N, 

125 grid_x, 

126 philox_seed, 

127 philox_offset, 

128 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

129 REDUCED: tl.constexpr = False, 

130 MASKED: tl.constexpr = True, 

131 FLAT: tl.constexpr = True, 

132 WIDE: tl.constexpr = False, 

133 FAST_LOG: tl.constexpr = True, 

134): 

135 rng_state = philox_offset.to(tl.int64) ^ philox_seed.to(tl.int64) 

136 # The raw per-call state must be avalanched before it is XOR-keyed into 

137 # the per-element hash input. Raw, the state only differs additively 

138 # between calls (offset advances by N/4), so s0_1 ^ s0_2 is a constant 

139 # small mask M: element i of call 2 then hashes input (i ^ M) ^ s0_1 -- 

140 # i.e. successive same-shape calls return the SAME multiset of samples, 

141 # merely permuted (device-verified: 40 histogram bins identical to the 

142 # last count across successive calls, which every per-call statistical 

143 # test misses). fmix32 makes the per-call key pseudorandom, so the 

144 # cross-call sample overlap drops from a structural invariant to a 

145 # ~2^-32 coincidence. Scalar prologue: ~11 ops once per program. 

146 s0 = _fmix32((rng_state ^ (rng_state >> 32)).to(tl.uint32)) 

147 # Grid form: this backend caps grid.x at 65535 programs, which previously 

148 # forced BLOCK-wide tiles for large N (grid.x*BLOCK*4 >= N). The program 

149 # axis now optionally splits in 2D (pid = x + y*grid_x), unlocking smaller 

150 # tiles for huge N. FLAT keeps the single-program-axis form with zero 

151 # prologue arithmetic: the runtime grid_x multiply sits on the per-CTA 

152 # serial pid chain and costs ~0.85% when grid_y==1 still pays it, so hosts 

153 # must pass FLAT=True for 1D launches. grid_x is do_not_specialize to 

154 # avoid per-shape recompiles. Per-element sample identity is preserved: 

155 # the hash input is the global element offset, independent of the grid 

156 # decomposition, so outputs match the 1D launch bitwise. 

157 if FLAT: 

158 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

159 else: 

160 pid = tl.program_id(0) + tl.program_id(1) * grid_x 

161 # WIDE: without the grid.x bound the program count for a launch is no 

162 # longer implicitly < 2^31/BLOCK, so element offsets past the int32 domain 

163 # (N > 2^31 - BLOCK*4) must be computed in int64 to avoid wrap-around 

164 # stores. Note the hash input truncates to uint32, capping the fresh- 

165 # sample offset domain at 2^32 elements per RNG state; the host arm only 

166 # guards the offset arithmetic, beyond 2^32 elements samples repeat. 

167 if WIDE: 

168 off_0 = pid.to(tl.int64) * (BLOCK * 4) + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

169 else: 

170 off_0 = pid * (BLOCK * 4) + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

171 off_1 = off_0 + BLOCK 

172 off_2 = off_1 + BLOCK 

173 off_3 = off_2 + BLOCK 

174 

175 if REDUCED: 

176 ha = _fmix32(off_0.to(tl.uint32) ^ s0) 

177 hb = _fmix32(off_2.to(tl.uint32) ^ s0) 

178 # angle integer in [0, 65535], radius uniform in [0, 1) 

179 w0 = (ha >> 16).to(tl.float32) 

180 u1 = tl.maximum(1.0e-7, (ha & 0xFFFF).to(tl.float32) * U16) 

181 w2 = (hb >> 16).to(tl.float32) 

182 u3 = tl.maximum(1.0e-7, (hb & 0xFFFF).to(tl.float32) * U16) 

183 # radius stays in the un-folded sqrt(-2*log(u)) form: the folded 

184 # variant cancels catastrophically as u -> 1 and can go NaN. 

185 ra = tl.sqrt(_neg_two_ln(u1, FAST_LOG)) 

186 rb = tl.sqrt(_neg_two_ln(u3, FAST_LOG)) 

187 # x = pi * (2u - 1) == u_int * (2*pi/2^16) - pi (exact fold, fma) 

188 x0 = tl.fma(w0, A16, -PI) 

189 x2 = tl.fma(w2, A16, -PI) 

190 s0_, c0_ = _sin_cos_reduced(x0) 

191 s2_, c2_ = _sin_cos_reduced(x2) 

192 else: 

193 h0 = _fmix32(off_0.to(tl.uint32) ^ s0) 

194 h1 = _fmix32(off_1.to(tl.uint32) ^ s0) 

195 h2 = _fmix32(off_2.to(tl.uint32) ^ s0) 

196 h3 = _fmix32(off_3.to(tl.uint32) ^ s0) 

197 w0 = (h0 >> 8).to(tl.float32) 

198 u1 = tl.maximum(1.0e-7, (h1 >> 8).to(tl.float32) * U24) 

199 w2 = (h2 >> 8).to(tl.float32) 

200 u3 = tl.maximum(1.0e-7, (h3 >> 8).to(tl.float32) * U24) 

201 ra = tl.sqrt(_neg_two_ln(u1, FAST_LOG)) 

202 rb = tl.sqrt(_neg_two_ln(u3, FAST_LOG)) 

203 # x = u_int * (2*pi/2^24) - pi (exact fold into the [-pi, pi) fit 

204 # domain of _sin_cos_reduced; full circle is preserved by symmetry) 

205 x0 = tl.fma(w0, A24, -PI) 

206 x2 = tl.fma(w2, A24, -PI) 

207 s0_, c0_ = _sin_cos_reduced(x0) 

208 s2_, c2_ = _sin_cos_reduced(x2) 

209 

210 if MASKED: 

211 tl.store(out_ptr + off_0, ra * c0_, mask=off_0 < N) 

212 tl.store(out_ptr + off_1, ra * s0_, mask=off_1 < N) 

213 tl.store(out_ptr + off_2, rb * c2_, mask=off_2 < N) 

214 tl.store(out_ptr + off_3, rb * s2_, mask=off_3 < N) 

215 else: 

216 tl.store(out_ptr + off_0, ra * c0_) 

217 tl.store(out_ptr + off_1, ra * s0_) 

218 tl.store(out_ptr + off_2, rb * c2_) 

219 tl.store(out_ptr + off_3, rb * s2_)

222device_ = device 

223 

224 

225def randn(size, *, dtype=None, layout=None, device=None, pin_memory=None): 

226 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME RANDN") 

227 if dtype is None: 

228 dtype = torch.get_default_dtype() 

229 if device is None: 

230 device = torch.device(device_.name) 

231 out = torch.empty(size, device=device, dtype=dtype) 

232 N = volume(size) 

233 # Post-Estrin rescan (GCU400, official do_bench kernel mode, median): 

234 # BLOCK=1024 still wins the latency band (4096 elems: 3.22us; 96000: 

235 # 3.54us) and keeps >= 24 CTAs of parallelism. Above it the optimum 

236 # moved with the shortened trig dependency chains: 

237 # 16-bit lane: B8192 up to 1Gi (16.7M fp16 115.7us vs 129.1 @4096), 

238 # B16384 beyond (1Gi fp16 6.90ms vs 7.12 @8192). 

239 # fp32 lane: B2048 up to 256Mi elements (16.7M fp32 120.1us vs 

240 # 129.0 @8192), B16384 beyond (1Gi fp32 6.94ms vs 

241 # 7.96 @8192). 

242 if N <= 1048576: 

243 BLOCK = 1024 

244 elif dtype == torch.float32: 

245 BLOCK = 2048 if N < 268435456 else 16384 

246 else: 

247 BLOCK = 8192 if N < 1073741824 else 16384 

248 total = triton.cdiv(N, BLOCK * UNROLL) 

249 if total <= 65535: 

250 grid = (total,) 

251 grid_x, flat = 0, True 

252 else: 

253 grid_y = triton.cdiv(total, 32768) 

254 grid_x = triton.cdiv(total, grid_y) 

255 grid = (grid_x, grid_y) 

256 flat = False 

257 increment = triton.cdiv(N, UNROLL) 

258 philox_seed, philox_offset = philox_backend_seed_offset(increment) 

259 with torch_device_fn.device(device): 

260 reduced = dtype != torch.float32 

261 # EVEN specialization: when N is an exact multiple of the per-program 

262 # tile the four bound compares per store group are dead weight 

263 # (~0.31 ms per 1Gi kernel); the masked kernel covers every other N. 

264 randn_kernel[grid]( 

265 out, 

266 N, 

267 grid_x, 

268 philox_seed, 

269 philox_offset, 

270 BLOCK=BLOCK, 

271 REDUCED=reduced, 

272 MASKED=N % (BLOCK * UNROLL) != 0, 

273 FLAT=flat, 

274 WIDE=N > 2**31 - BLOCK * UNROLL, 

275 FAST_LOG=dtype != torch.float32, 

276 num_warps=4, 

277 ) 

278 return out
